title: Backup scope, frequency, retention and location
status_rationale: No production data, backup system or restore test exists as of 2026-11-25; backup design appears only in Unbound requirements.
target_answer: All authoritative stores are backed up at frequencies meeting their data-class RPO: continuous write-ahead-log archiving plus daily snapshots for the ledger database, versioned object storage for issued documents, and daily backups of configuration and source repositories. Rebuildable projections, search indexes and embeddings are excluded by design and rebuilt from the journal. Backups are retained at least 35 days for operational recovery, with longer retention for financial records governed by the retention policy, and copies are kept in a second location within the tenant's residency jurisdiction. Customers may also take their own complete, verifiable export at any time.
intended_practice: Configure backups with the first production-like environment; generate the inventory from configuration.
customer_statement: No production backups exist because no production system exists. Our design covers all authoritative data with frequencies set by data class.

title: Backup protection: immutability, separation, encryption and access
status_rationale: No production data, backup system or restore test exists as of 2026-11-25; backup design appears only in Unbound requirements.
target_answer: Backups are written to a vault in a separate cloud account with separate credentials and a compliance-mode retention lock, so no production administrator, compromised credential or AI agent can delete or alter them during retention. Backups are encrypted with keys outside production key scope, with an escrowed recovery path tested annually. Restores into production require two authorized people and are logged as tamper-evident evidence; agents cannot initiate them. Second person: a production restore is authorized by the managing member and a contracted operator (the same party named for break-glass). Until one exists, restores run only through the pipeline with automatic notification of affected tenants' administrators and post-restore review by the contracted reviewer.
current_practice: Not established. SOC2-006 and UNB-DATA-008 require protected, independent backup storage.
intended_practice: Adopt a separate backup account and retention lock from the first environment.
customer_statement: We plan immutable, encrypted backups held in a separate account that production administrators cannot delete. Not yet implemented.

challenge.customer_intent: Make sure an attacker or rogue insider cannot destroy both production data and its backups.
challenge.adverse_outcome: Ransomware or malicious deletion leaves no recoverable copy.
challenge.conventional_control_effectiveness: Policy-based restrictions on backup deletion are routinely defeated by compromised administrator credentials; questionnaires accept 'backups are encrypted' without asking who can delete them.
challenge.legally_required: No statute for Echelon. EU DORA Article 12 requires EU financial entities to keep backups physically and logically segregated; NYDFS Part 500 as amended requires covered entities to maintain backups protected from unauthorized alteration.
challenge.contractually_required: Increasingly in cyber insurance applications and bank contracts.
challenge.architectural_elimination: Deletion within the retention period is eliminated in scope by compliance-mode retention lock in a separate account.
challenge.automatic_enforcement: Enforced by the storage service, not by procedure.
challenge.continuous_evidence: Daily automated read of vault configuration and principals with delete permission.
challenge.stronger_alternative: Structural immutability with continuous configuration evidence instead of an annual attestation.
challenge.customer_acceptance_likelihood: Unknown; unvalidated. The prior agent judgment is kept in supporting_arguments.
challenge.invalidating_conditions: If the separate account shares an identity provider or organization root that the attacker controls.
challenge.alternative_risks: Immutable retention complicates honoring deletion requests before expiry.
supporting_arguments: Defeats the most common ransomware recovery failure.
agent judgment: customer acceptance likelihood 'Likely.'; institutional acceptance rating 'likely' (unvalidated, no cited source).
opposing_arguments: Privacy regulators may question retention of deleted personal data in locked backups.

Institutional acceptance is unvalidated: no buyer, auditor, regulator or insurer evidence or cited source supports an acceptance rating (DD-VAL-ADV-001, DD-VAL-ADV-002). Treat any rating as agent judgment until target-customer conversations or a sourced document support it.

residual_risks: As of 2026-11-25 no second authorized person for restores exists.

title: Restore testing and integrity verification
status_rationale: No production data, backup system or restore test exists as of 2026-11-25; backup design appears only in Unbound requirements.
target_answer: Restores of each data class run at least quarterly into isolated environments and are verified by hash-chain or signed-checkpoint verification, record counts and per-fund trial balances, not only by job success. Missing or failed backups raise monitored control exceptions. Results are retained as evidence and summarized for customers under NDA.
current_practice: Not established. UNB-DATA-012 requires integrity verification that detects omitted, altered, duplicated and reordered records, including after restore.
intended_practice: Implement integrity verification with the ledger; schedule restore tests from the first pre-production environment.
customer_statement: No restore tests have been performed. We plan quarterly restore tests verified against cryptographic checkpoints and trial balances.

title: Point-in-time recovery and deterministic replay
status_rationale: No production data, backup system or restore test exists as of 2026-11-25; backup design appears only in Unbound requirements.
target_answer: The authoritative ledger is strictly append-only; corrections are new linked records, never updates. Point-in-time recovery is available to the second within the retention window through write-ahead-log archiving, and every balance and projection can be reconstructed by deterministic replay of the journal to any prior point. Replay is side-effect free: it cannot send payments, emails or provider calls. Replay equivalence against live projections is tested monthly.
current_practice: Not established. ACC-MDL-002 (append-only journals), ACC-MDL-007 (idempotent posting, replay without duplicate effects) and UNB-IMM-010 (load tests for historical replay) specify the design.
intended_practice: Build the ledger as append-only with typed separation of replay from effect dispatch.
customer_statement: Our ledger design is append-only so that state can be reconstructed by replaying history without re-sending payments. Not yet built or tested.

challenge.customer_intent: Be able to recover data as of a specific time, for example just before an erroneous bulk change.
challenge.adverse_outcome: Erroneous changes cannot be unwound precisely; history is lost.
challenge.conventional_control_effectiveness: Point-in-time database restore recovers state but discards everything after the restore point, including legitimate later transactions, and requires manual re-entry.
challenge.legally_required: No. Record-keeping rules such as SEC Rule 17a-4 bind broker-dealer customers, not Echelon.
challenge.historical_convention: Nightly backups plus transaction log shipping.
challenge.architectural_elimination: Destructive overwrite of financial history is eliminated in scope by append-only design; an erroneous change is reversed with a new record rather than a restore.
challenge.automatic_enforcement: Database permissions and ledger API deny update and delete on posted entries.
challenge.stronger_alternative: Correction by compensating entries plus replay, with database restore reserved for infrastructure loss.
challenge.customer_acceptance_likelihood: Unknown; unvalidated. The prior agent judgment is kept in supporting_arguments.
challenge.invalidating_conditions: If any authoritative state lives outside the journal, or replay depends on mutable reference data that was not versioned.
challenge.alternative_risks: Replay time grows with history; requires snapshots and load testing.
supporting_arguments: agent judgment: customer acceptance likelihood 'Likely among finance and audit buyers.'; institutional acceptance rating 'likely' (unvalidated, no cited source).
opposing_arguments: Append-only does not protect against infrastructure loss; backups remain necessary.
Replay performance at large scale is unproven.

Institutional acceptance is unvalidated: no buyer, auditor, regulator or insurer evidence or cited source supports an acceptance rating (DD-VAL-ADV-001, DD-VAL-ADV-002). Treat any rating as agent judgment until target-customer conversations or a sourced document support it.

title: Backups, retention, legal hold and deletion
status_rationale: No production data, backup system or restore test exists as of 2026-11-25; backup design appears only in Unbound requirements.
target_answer: Backups honor the retention policy, including the seven-year minimum for financial records and legal holds. When personal data is deleted or a tenant exits, Echelon states which backups still contain the data and when they expire (no more than 35 days after the exit package is delivered for operational backups), and the destruction certificate lists residual copies and records retained by legal obligation. Echelon does not claim cryptographic erasure where plaintext remains in backups, logs or exports.
current_practice: Not established. RR-UNB-TEN-016-r1, UNB-IMM-008, REQ-X-036 and SOC2-032 define the policy.
intended_practice: Implement retention policy engine and backup expiry tracking before production.
customer_statement: We plan to disclose how long data persists in backups after deletion and to issue destruction certificates listing any residual copies. Not yet implemented.
